subject: Clarify: Pen test coverage & ownership for Hosted / Dedicated / Private (LedgerPay Audit)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@ledgerpay.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test artifacts + scope question for LedgerPay audit

Hi Karthik,

Quick one — our audit team needs the most recent penetration test artifacts and an explicit statement of what hosting variants are covered for LedgerPay. Specifically:

- Is Redwood's most recent pen test covering customer workloads running on Hosted API? Dedicated pools that LedgerPay has reserved?
- For Private/VPC deployments, do the pen test results cover customer-managed runtime (i.e., customer deploys Redwood runtime into their VPC/on-prem), or only Redwood-managed Private instances?

We want to include a short paragraph in our SIG that clearly says which pieces are within Redwood's testing boundary versus where LedgerPay is responsible. If you can attach the summary plus a simple ownership matrix (component -> who is responsible / in-scope), that would be ideal.

Thanks — can you reply by EOD tomorrow? The compliance window is tight.

—Daniel
Security Lead, LedgerPay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts + scope question for LedgerPay audit

Daniel —

Thanks for the note. Short answer up front: Hosted API and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools are in-scope of our most recent third-party penetration test. Customer-managed Private deployments (where the customer deploys the serving runtime and manages the VPC/on-prem environment) are out-of-scope for Redwood's penetration test; in those cases LedgerPay retains responsibility for the perimeter and host-level controls.

I've attached a one-page summary and a scope matrix that maps components to ownership. Key points to pull into your SIG:

- Hosted (redwood.ai hosted API): covered by our full pen test (control plane + serving runtime + network edges).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity managed by Redwood): covered (same level as Hosted) — includes the dedicated GPU pools, our orchestration layer, and the control plane.
- Private (Redwood-managed Private deployment): covered for components that Redwood manages (control plane, update channels, any managed bastions).
- Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem): NOT covered — customer is responsible for host hardening, VPC ACLs, and any self-hosted connectors.

Two operational caveats:
1) If LedgerPay uses a Redwood-managed VPN or Data Connector that terminates in Redwood infrastructure, that connector is included.
2) Agent/sidecar code that runs inside a customer-controlled network will not be tested by our vendor unless Redwood has explicit, test-time access; we can scope that in via a supplementary engagement if you need it.

I'll leave Laura and Monica on-copy for any additional artifact requests or a signed statement for SIG/CAIQ. If helpful, we can provide a short paragraph for your SIG template.

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_summary.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB), scope_matrix_v2.xlsx (Excel)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerpay.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:23:00 -07:00

Karthik — thanks, that helps. Two follow-ups from our audit:

1) Can you provide a concise, SOC2/audit-friendly sentence we can paste into our SIG that says "Which hosting variants are covered"?
2) We need confirmation whether the pen test included any testing of the administrative control plane endpoints that Authenticate via our SSO integration (i.e., SAML/OIDC flows) when used against Dedicated instances.

If the control plane auth pieces are in-scope, we'll include that in our SIG. If not, please call that out.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Daniel

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Daniel —

Following up for the audit team with the specific wording you requested and the auth clarification. Please see the two bullet points below — feel free to paste directly into your SIG/CAIQ answer.

- Audit-friendly statement (suggested): "Redwood Inference's most recent third-party penetration test covers Redwood-operated control plane components, serving runtime, and network edges for Hosted API and Redwood-managed Dedicated capacity. Customer-managed Private or on-prem deployments are out of scope unless Redwood explicitly accepts and documents those deployments for testing."

- Auth/control-plane clarification: "Administrative control plane endpoints (including SSO/SAML/OIDC flows) are in-scope for Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated deployments and were exercised during the assessment. For customer-managed Private deployments, control plane testing is limited to Redwood-managed components; SSO endpoints terminating inside a customer-controlled network were not tested unless Redwood had explicit test access documented in the engagement scope."

If you need a signed attestation on Redwood letterhead, we can route that through Legal — let us know and we'll get it to you within 48 hours. Monica — can you add the signed one-pager to the shared Drive link and share view-only access to LedgerPay?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Security | Redwood Inference
